bib.title: Efficient Guided Generation for Large Language Models

question: How can text generation from an LLM be constrained to a regular expression or context-free grammar without scanning the whole vocabulary at every step?
hypothesis: Recasting generation as transitions between finite-state-machine states lets an index over the vocabulary give the allowed-token mask in O(1) on average, so guided generation adds little overhead.
contributions: An FSM formulation of regex-guided generation with Algorithms 3 and 4 building a map from FSM states to allowed vocabulary subsets
An extension sketch to CFGs via LALR(1) parsers and pushdown automata, with a trie-based index
The open source Python library Outlines implementing the approach
A single timing comparison against the Guidance library

method.summary: Boolean-mask the next-token distribution so only tokens that keep the output inside a regex/CFG language have non-zero probability. Precompute a map sigma from each FSM state to the vocabulary strings accepted from that state, so the mask is a hash lookup. Evaluated by three qualitative GPT2-medium examples and one runtime plot against Guidance on GPT-2.

other.use: Section 3.2 timing comparison, device cuda, temperature 0.1; parameter count not stated

inference.decoding: multinomial sampling from the masked categorical distribution (Algorithm 2); temperature 0.1 in the timing test; decoding for the Section 3.1 examples not stated
inference.max_tokens: 30 in Section 3.1 examples; varied in Section 3.2 (plot x axis 5 to 100 generated tokens, read from the figure)
inference.samples: Section 3.2: one sample per max_tokens value (timeit, single loop, single repeat). Section 3.1: one output per prompt. No seeds stated.
inference.prompting: Zero-shot raw prompts, e.g. 'Is 1+1=2? ', 'In what year was Noam Chomsky born?\n', 'What is the IP address of the Google DNS servers? ', 'What is a good Python variable name? '

parameters.guidance_settings: token_healing=False, device=cuda, temperature=0.1, caching=False, async_mode=False, stream=False

other.hardware_timing: device cuda; GPU model not stated
other.index_size: around 50 MB for a slightly augmented Python grammar, naively built with un-reduced DFAs (Section 5)
other.cost: O(N) per token for the naive approach, O(1) on average for the index; index construction cost called 'effectively irrelevant', memory theoretically |Q|

metrics.name: runtime
metrics.definition: wall time of one generation call timed with timeit, as a function of max_tokens

baselines: Guidance library (partial regex matching from the start of the sequence each step, iterating over the vocabulary)
eval.protocol: One run per max_tokens value, no repeats, no variance, one regex, one prompt. No accuracy, validity or quality measurement.

prompts.text: What is a good Python variable name?{{{{gen temperature=0.1 max_tokens={max_tokens} pattern="[^\W\d]\w*"}}}}
What is a good Python variable name?
In what year was Noam Chomsky born?\n
What is the IP address of the Google DNS servers?

evidence.quote: only one sample is collected for each value of max_tokens

results.claim: Masking with a precomputed state-to-vocabulary hash map costs O(1) on average per token, versus a fixed O(N) vocabulary scan for the usual approach.
results.setup: Argued analytically for regex FSMs with a hash-map index sigma; no benchmark of the lookup itself.
results.quote: The result is an algorithm that costs O(1) on average.
results.note: The paper hedges: 'Using a hash-map for σ can make the m step in Algorithm 2 cost only O(1) on average'.

results.claim: In the one timing test, Guidance's runtime grows steeply with the max generated tokens while Outlines stays far lower; the paper gives no numbers, only a plot.
results.setup: GPT-2 (N = 50,257), regex [^\W\d]\w*, prompt 'What is a good Python variable name?', temperature 0.1, cuda, one sample per max_tokens, Guidance has no point past 60 tokens (read from Fig. in Section 3.2).
results.quote: the observed scaling in the maximum number of sampled tokens is striking and is indicative of the growing computational problem implied by the approach.
results.note: Read from the plot: Guidance about 118 s at 60 tokens; Outlines about 1 to 2 s at 100 tokens and rising slightly, so 'flat' is approximate. The authors add 'Barring any configuration oversights that might be creating a large run-time discrepancy'.

results.claim: A naively built index for a slightly augmented Python grammar is about 50 MB.
results.setup: Slightly augmented Python grammar, un-reduced DFAs, unused and redundant parser/FSM configurations included; model/vocabulary not stated.

results.claim: With GPT2-medium, regex-guided output obeys the pattern while unguided output rambles; the guided yes/no answer 'Always' to 'Is 1+1=2?' is valid in shape only.
results.setup: GPT2-medium (355M), Outlines generate.regex, max_tokens=30, one output per prompt, shown as illustration.
results.note: The paper does not comment that the answer is wrong; the Chomsky example returns 1952 (a plausible but unchecked year) and the Google DNS example returns 2.2.6.1.

results.claim: The paper reports no accuracy or task-quality measurement of guided versus unguided generation.
results.quote: One could, for instance, attempt to quantify the discrepancy between the masked logits generated by our method and the raw logits generated by the model.

limits: Only one timing test: one regex, one prompt, GPT-2, one sample per length, one baseline (Guidance), GPU model unspecified, no variance.
Authors concede possible 'configuration oversights' in the Guidance comparison.
No accuracy, validity, or quality results; the effect of masking on output quality is left as future work.
CFG/LALR(1)/PDA extension is described but not benchmarked or fully specified (sketch only); no results for JSON or Python grammars apart from the 50 MB index remark.
Memory cost is theoretical |Q| and only measured as about 50 MB for one grammar.
Index construction cost dismissed as 'effectively irrelevant' with no measurement.
Guidance behaviour is as of July 2023 and has since changed; Outlines API shown (outlines.text.generate) is the old one.
